2) Hosted quickstart asks I flagged for our ops team: sandbox endpoints, rateband limits during trial, and prefix/KV prefetch suggestions for your low-latency use case.

3) Security/data: you mentioned SOC2 and simple egress controls; noted — we can provide SOC2 evidence and a data handling summary during the sandbox setup.

Next steps I propose (attached action list):

- Quick technical call (30m) to map endpoints to your staging flows — Jordan can lead.

Are you comfortable with that plan? If yes I will: provision the sandbox, share the sandbox credentials, and schedule the endpoint-mapping call.

Thanks — Camila

Hi Camila — appreciate the recap. Quick answers and two clarifying questions: 

1) Yes, Hosted for the pilot is our preference. We want to validate latency and cost before considering Dedicated.

2) The soft rateband you suggested looks reasonable, but can you clarify how token-level throttling vs request-level throttling works in practice? For our use case (short chat turns + embeddings for search), bursts of embedding requests will come from a nightly job — we need to avoid dropped requests.

3) Data residency: we need to keep pilot data in us-east-1 and want to understand how long logs are retained during the trial (30 vs 90 days).

Can Jordan or ops confirm the above two points? Also, please mark the mutual action plan item that shows the rollback/fallback (if we hit soft limits).

Thanks — Alejandra

Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick follow-ups + sample next steps for Hosted eval

Hi Alejandra — Jordan here from Ops. Quick answers and a recommended pilot config below.

How limits work (short):
- Request-level throttling: a per-endpoint cap on concurrent requests (we set concurrency guard at 3 for the sandbox).
- Token-level throttling: a per-account token throughput ceiling over sliding windows (prevents cost runaway on very long generations).
- Both apply: a request can be rejected if either limit is exceeded; we favor request-level rejections on microbursts and token ceilings on sustained higher-throughput.

Avoiding dropped embedding bursts (recommended):
- For nightly embedding jobs, we recommend batching at 200-500 vectors per request where possible and enabling our background ingestion queue (ops-offered during sandbox). That queue accepts bursts and drains at the endpoint's throughput while returning an ingestion id so you can poll status.
- Alternatively, schedule the job into a short maintenance window where the sandbox rateband is raised temporarily (we can set a scheduled burst window).

Pilot config (proposed):
- Region: us-east-1 (confirmed).
- Endpoint slice: 1 chat+generation endpoint + a separate embedding endpoint.
- Soft rateband: 60 reqs/min per endpoint; concurrency guard: 3 concurrent requests.
- Token ceiling: 2M tokens rolling per hour for the sandbox account.
- Prefetch / KV cache: enable prefix KV caching for chat sessions (saves ~30% token costs on repeated prefixes). Good for your re-used prompts.
- Log retention: 30 days (we can extend if needed; default for trials is 30).

Fallback/rollback: if we hit soft limits we will automatically: 1) queue excess embedding jobs to the background ingestion queue (no data loss), 2) return a 429 for non-idempotent requests if concurrency saturated and provide a Retry-After header, and 3) notify both teams and propose a scheduled burst window or temporary uplift to Dedicated capacity if sustained.

Next actions I will take today: provision the sandbox slice in us-east-1, share the sandbox keys, and add a scheduled 30m endpoint-mapping call (Camila to coordinate timing). Attached sample rate matrix for your review.

Jordan Blake | Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
